sections.html:
Up on Crowley's Ridge in the northeast corner of the state, Jonesboro splits the Craighead County seat duties with Lake City. By land area, at about 80.7 square miles, it is the second-biggest city in Arkansas. The 2025 estimate is 83,296 residents, up from 78,576 in 2020 and 55,515 in 2000, and the metro area holds about 139,440 people.

Growth means new subdivisions on the edges while the oldest houses sit near downtown, so a seller in an older part of town competes with newer construction. The city limits contain six public school districts: Jonesboro, Valley View, Nettleton, Westside Consolidated, Bay and Brookland. Your house could be zoned to any of them, so look up the address before you quote a school to a buyer.

The city's growth also means more homes are competing for the same buyers. Price your house by looking at what actually sells in your part of town, and be honest about condition.

Work here centers on Arkansas State University, the biggest single employer, along with health care, agriculture, retail and manufacturing. St. Bernards Regional Medical Center and NEA Baptist both operate here, and the region treats Jonesboro as its hospital hub. Students and staff from the A-State campus, which also hosts the NYIT College of Osteopathic Medicine, rent or buy close by. Steady university and hospital jobs support a deep pool of renters, which helps a landlord who is weighing a sale.

Landlords can sell with the tenants in place. Share the lease and rent figures early.

Tornadoes are part of the local record. A 1968 F4 (May 15 to 16) destroyed 164 homes, and another F4 followed on May 27, 1973. On March 28, 2020, an EF3 tornado with peak winds around 140 mph swept across the south and east sides, damaging houses, hangars at the airport and the Turtle Creek mall.

Expect questions about roof age, storm shelters, insurance claims and permits. A house fixed after the 2020 storm should come with the contractor's paperwork, so dig it out first. Annual precipitation runs about 52 inches, so roofs and drainage get a close look either way.

The city pushes owners to clean up blighted property through neighborhood sweeps and a boarding and securing ordinance. Sweeps look for tall grass, vehicles that do not run, unsanitary conditions and unlawful storage. A first visit brings a warning, and a second pass can bring a court citation.

The boarding rule kicks in when a vacant building goes 60 days without connected utilities. Broken doors and windows have seven days to be secured, and the owner has six months from notice to repair, rehabilitate or demolish. Fines start at $100 per day, and failure to act can lead to abatement, condemnation or a citation. Code enforcement answers at 870-933-4658.

Sellers most often land under this rule through an empty inherited house. If you sell before the six months end, the repair burden passes to the buyer.

If a code notice arrives on a house you want to sell, do not ignore it. Fines of $100 per day add up quickly, and a buyer's title search will turn up an open citation. Responding early, even to say the house is for sale, keeps the problem from growing.

sections.h2: If you inherited a vacant house
sections.html:
Utilities get shut off, the grass grows, and the 60-day clock in the boarding ordinance starts ticking without anyone noticing. Handling an estate? Start here:

  • Find out who has legal authority to sign.
  • Keep the doors and windows secured so no violation can start.
  • Get the tax balance from the collector and ask the title company about liens.
  • Call code enforcement at 870-933-4658 if you already received a notice.

A cash buyer taking the house in its current state can close before the six-month window ends, so you skip the repairs the notice would demand.

Interstate 555 and five state and federal highways cross Jonesboro: AR 1, AR 18, US 49, US 63 and US 78. GOJO, the city's transit system, runs four fixed bus routes and paratransit, and Greyhound offers intercity service. The municipal airport has commercial flights through the federal Essential Air Service program, and Crowley's Ridge Parkway, the state's first National Scenic Byway, passes through the city.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates and penalties
sections.html:
The Craighead County Collector takes payment from the first business day of March through October 15 of the year after assessment. Tax unpaid after October 15 carries a 10 percent penalty, and interest on delinquent real estate tax accrues daily. A check in the mail is on time if the postmark is October 15 or earlier.

Collector officeAddress and phone
Jonesboro511 Union Street, Suite 107, 72401; (870) 933-4560
Lake City107 Cobean

Arkansas reappraises real property on four-year cycles under Act 139 of 2023, and a homestead's taxable value can rise only 5 percent a year. To contest a valuation formally, schedule a hearing with the county board of equalization by the third Monday in August. The state's real property transfer tax is $3.30 per $1,000 of consideration, and the deed is recorded at the county clerk.

You can still sell with delinquent tax. The balance is deducted from your sale proceeds by the title company, so get the collector's payoff figure first. Interest accrues daily, so the number changes from week to week.

When you sign an offer, the title company checks ownership and liens and drafts the settlement statement, which lays out the tax payoff, mortgage balance, transfer tax and your net. Afterward the clerk records the deed. Cash deals skip the lender appraisal, so the calendar hinges on the title search. Listings stack showings, financing and an appraisal on top.

Pack a folder with the deed, a photo ID, the latest tax bill and storm-repair paperwork, plus the lease and current rent if tenants live there.

sections.h2: Ways to sell a Jonesboro house
sections.html:
Sellers choose among a listing, a sale by owner and a cash offer. An updated house and a flexible calendar favor a listing, though lender financing, inspections and appraisals can stretch the timeline by weeks. A cash deal closes when you say it will.

  • Storm-repaired or older: an as-is sale ends the repair haggling.
  • Vacant property: selling lets you avoid ongoing code citations.
  • Rental: ask whether the buyer will honor the lease.
  • Back taxes: get the collector's payoff first.

faqs.a: The 2025 estimate is 83,296 residents, which makes Jonesboro the fifth-largest city in Arkansas.

faqs.q: Is Jonesboro in a tornado-prone area?
faqs.a: Yes. The city has had F4 tornadoes in 1968 and 1973 and an EF3 tornado on March 28, 2020. Buyers often ask about roof age and storm repairs.

faqs.q: When are Craighead County property taxes due?
faqs.a: By October 15 of the year after assessment. After that date a 10 percent penalty applies, and interest on delinquent real estate tax accrues daily.

faqs.q: Can I sell a vacant, damaged house in Jonesboro?
faqs.a: Yes. A building with no utilities for 60 days can trigger the city's boarding and securing rules, so many owners sell before the six-month repair window ends.

faqs.q: What is the Arkansas real estate transfer tax?
faqs.a: It is $3.30 per $1,000 of consideration on deeds that convey real property for more than $100.
